title: Index Optimization
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and main trade-off of index optimization.
Apply index optimization to a small MongoDB data or operational scenario.
Verify the expected result, one edge case, and the relevant version/deployment assumption.

content.intro: Learn index optimization as part of MongoDB Indexes. The lesson preserves the PDF subtopics, connects them to a practical MongoDB pattern, and ends with a verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Index Optimization is a performance decision, not a rule to apply blindly. Start from a representative query and data distribution, inspect explain() evidence, and compare read improvements with write, memory and storage overhead.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the behavior you want, identify the collection/document shape and access pattern involved, then select the smallest MongoDB operation that expresses the requirement. Write down read/write patterns and negative cases, then test the proposal with representative data.

content_blocks.code:
db.products.createIndex({ category: 1, price: 1 });
db.products.find({ category: "stationery", price: { $lt: 10 } }).explain("executionStats");
content_blocks.expected_output: The index is evaluated against a category-and-price query; explain output, not the mere existence of an index, is the evidence.
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf displays this example as a reference and does not execute a MongoDB server or arbitrary driver code in the page. Run shell examples with mongosh, or driver examples in a separately configured Node.js/Python lab, against a disposable database. Verify installed server/driver versions and deployment feature availability first. Never place credentials in source files.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Use a dedicated training database and synthetic fixtures. Remove only objects created by this lesson or recreate the disposable database after confirming the target; do not run destructive/reset commands against production.

content_blocks.title: Environment and safety note
content_blocks.text: All examples are teaching references, not production-ready configuration. MongoDB Atlas-specific Search, Vector Search, monitoring, backup and automation features are marked as deployment-dependent. Server, driver, shell and managed-service capabilities differ; check the official documentation that matches your target.

content.task: Try it yourself: Capture explain("executionStats") for a representative query, compare an appropriate index or pipeline change, and record the read/write trade-off rather than guessing. Submit your choice plus the expected result/evidence and one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate the key idea in Index Optimization.
Predict the result and state how you would verify it.
Name one boundary, risk or version/deployment assumption.
hints: First, explain what “Index Optimization” needs to accomplish in this scenario.
Write down the data shape, filter, expected output or operational evidence before running the example.
Test one normal case and one meaningful boundary/failure case; consult the matching official reference.

common_mistakes.problem: Designing from an example instead of real access patterns
common_mistakes.why: A model, validator or index that fits one sample may fail for growth, optional values or important queries.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down read/write patterns and negative cases, then test the proposal with representative data.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a static reference result proves the environment will behave identically.
common_mistakes.why: MongoDB server, shell, driver, managed service and permissions can affect the available behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the target versions and privileges, run the smallest safe test, and keep expected and actual results side by side.

summary: Index Optimization is a performance decision, not a rule to apply blindly. Start from a representative query and data distribution, inspect explain() evidence, and compare read improvements with write, memory and storage overhead.
The supplied roadmap identifies these subtopics: Compound-index design; Balancing read and write performance; Index size management; Reviewing indexes against production queries.
Use a disposable practice environment, verify the result and keep operational assumptions explicit.
